课程简介（中文）

中世纪并不“黑暗”，却是孕育现代大学和博雅通识教育（liberal arts）的真正摇篮。古英语与中古英语文学不仅是英国文学的起点，也是深入理解英国乃至欧洲中世纪历史与文化的宝贵钥匙。本课程将以横贯盎格鲁—撒克逊时期至中世纪晚期的一系列文化问题为脉络，以众多古英语和中古英语经典文学作品为载体，以文本细读、问题串讲、翻译作注（annotated translation）练习、衍生观画（影）、课堂讨论为主要教学方式，引领学生进入中世纪文学、艺术、历史和思想的厚重而绮丽的世界。

 

课程简介（英文）

The Middle Ages were not a "dark" period, but rather the true cradle of modern universities and liberal arts education. Old English and Middle English literature not only mark the origins of English literature but also serve as invaluable keys to a deeper understanding of medieval history and culture in Britain and Europe.

This course will explore a series of cultural issues spanning the Anglo-Saxon period to the late Middle Ages, using classic works of Old and Middle English literature as primary texts. Through close reading, thematic lectures, annotated translation exercises, derivative viewing of artworks (and films), and classroom discussions, students will be guided into the rich and magnificent world of medieval literature, art, history, and thought.

 

教学目标

This course aims to open a window into medieval English literature and culture through close reading of texts in English. By engaging with the works of unnamed yet brilliant writers from the golden age of vernacular literature, students will explore the depth and allure of medieval language and literary traditions. The course bridges classical antiquity and the early modern period, fostering a well-rounded humanistic education rooted in the classical and medieval ideals of erudition. Additionally, it cultivates interdisciplinary and cross-linguistic competencies—grounded in English—through comprehensive study, textual analysis, and critical discussion.

教学方式

The course consists of fifteen lecture sessions (2 hours each) paired with in-class group discussions. Periodic annotated translation exercises will be assigned throughout the term.

 The course also includes optional film screenings (on-campus) and museum/gallery visits (off-campus, subject to availability) as supplementary activities.

教学内容与进度安排

Course Content (subject to change depending on actual progress)

 

Week 1. Introduction to Anglo-Saxon History and Literacy

Essential reading：

  1. Caedmun’s Hymn (from Bede’s Ecclesiastical History)
  2. Exeter Book Riddles 47 & 60

Selective reading:

  1. More Exeter Book riddles
  2. Bede’s Ecclesiastical History of the English People (I)

Week 2. Faith and Conversion: Runic Writings

Essential reading：

  1. The Fate of Apostles (excerpt)
  2. Christ II (fragments)
  3. Riddle 42

Selective reading:

  1. Dream of the Rood
  2. Bede’s Ecclesiastical History of the English People (II)

Week 3. Other Spaces, Humanoids, Monsters

Essential reading：

  1. Beowulf Manuscript: Wonders of the East
  2. Riddle 30a

Selective reading:

  1. Deor
  2. The Phoenix
  3. Bede’s Ecclesiastical History of the English People (III, IV)

Week 4. Hall and Anti-halls: Seascape and Ruins

Essential reading：

  1. The Seafarer
  2. The Ruin

Selective reading:

  1. The Wanderer
  2. Bede’s Ecclesiastical History of the English People (V)

Week 5. Women’s Voices in Anglo-Saxon Society

Essential reading：

  1. The Wife’s Lament
  2. Wulf and Eadwacer

Selective reading:

  1. The Husband’s Message
  2. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicles （I, II）

Week 6. Germanic Heroic Codes

Essential reading:

  1. “Cynewulf and Cyneheard” (from Anglo-Saxon Chronicles)
  2. Tacitus’ Germania

 Selective reading:

  1. The Battle of Brunanburh
  2. The Battle of Maldon

Week 7 Lores, Charms, Wisdom

Essential readings:

  1. Maxims I, II
  2. Selected metrical charms

Selective reading:

  1. Beowulf Manuscript: Alexander’s Letter to Aristotle
  2. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicles（III）

Week 8. Scops and Minstrels, Story and History

   Essential reading: “Finnsburg Episode” (from Beowulf)

Selective reading: Beowulf, the complete poem

Week 9. Midterm examination

 

Week 10. The Fourteenth Century and Middle English Ascendancy

 Essential reading: “General Prologue”, from Canterbury Tales

Selective reading: The Squire’s Tale

Week 11. Astrology, Music, Science

Essential readings: The Franklin’s Tale

Selective reading:

  1. Chaucer’s Treatise on the Astrolabe
  2. The Wife of Bath’s Tale

Week 12. Death, Last Things, Seven Cardinal Sins

Essential readings: The Pardoner’s Tale

Selective reading: The Prioress’ Tale

Week 13. Fairies, Madness, Otherworld, Romance

Essential readings: Sir Orfeo

Selective reading:

  1. Sir Gawain and the Green Knight (Fit I, II)
  2. R.R.Tolkien: On Fairy-stories

Week 14. Chivalric Adventures and Courtly Love

Essential readings: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight （excerpt）

Selective reading: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight (Fit III, IV)

Week 15. Middle English Lyrical Tradition and Victorian Medievalism

Essential readings: Selected Middle English Lyrics

Selective reading: Selected texts from Samuel Coleridge, John Keats and Alfred Tennyson

Week 16. Final Assignment (Submission in Class)

 

Depending on experts' availabiblity, this course will also include 3-4 sessions taught by an invited expert (Chinese or foreign) in related field, in order to give the students a more thorough understanding of the materials via different teaching methods.
